page.title: Flexible theme customization
page.subtitle: One seed moves the whole system. Pick a palette and every control, surface, mark and focus ring on the board below repaints in place.

welcome.description: Give the generator a brand colour and it writes the seed file, measures every contrast pair and refuses the ones that miss.

chat.answer: The seed is scoped to the board, so the rest of the document keeps its own palette.

thought.label: How the seed was applied
thought.contrastBody: Label on fill and fill on canvas, both themes, against WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 and SC 1.4.11.

alert.title: Check
alert.description: The custom seed is applied as authored. Nothing lifts a light seed onto the dark spine, so a brand that has to read on both canvases needs a second value measured against the dark one.

themeEditor.title: Theme editor
themeEditor.subtitle: One seed colour in, a whole brand out, measured rather than asserted.

unreadable.title: The token stylesheet could not be read
unreadable.description: This page derives a brand from the canvas colours and ramp steps the document is painting, read from the live stylesheet. Neither could be read here, so nothing below it would be a measurement.

order.title: Seed, then role, then scope, then instance
order.description: Stop at the first level that does the job. Every level below the seed is a value that has stopped deriving, and nothing tells you when the brand moves past it.

seed.title: 1. Seed
seed.description: The brand's action colour: what a primary button is filled with. In most cases this is the whole theme.
seed.label: Brand seed
seed.helper: A six digit hex. Everything below derives from it and is measured against WCAG 2.2 AA.
seed.presetHelper: Each of these produces an answer a well behaved blue hides.

preset.very-light: Near white: the fill cannot clear the light canvas
preset.very-dark: Near black: the dark seed runs to white
preset.sunflower: Sunflower: repoints the state steps in both themes

announce.one: Seed {hex}. Light {light}, dark {dark}. {pass} of {count} measured pair clears AA.
announce.other: Seed {hex}. Light {light}, dark {dark}. {pass} of {count} measured pairs clear AA.

seed.announceNoDark: Seed {hex}. No lightness at this hue and saturation carries a readable fill on the dark canvas, so there is no dark theme to measure.

derived.title: 2. What the seed produces
derived.description: Read only, because these are results. Three roles per theme are written into the export; the rest derive from the primary in scope at the element that paints them, so writing them would pin them to this seed.

contrast.title: 3. Contrast
contrast.description: Every pair the seed produces, measured with the package's own WCAG helper. A label on its fill owes 4.5:1 (SC 1.4.3); a fill on the canvas behind it owes 3:1 (SC 1.4.11).

overrides.title: 4. Per token overrides
overrides.description: Below the seed on purpose. Reach for one only when the seed is right and a single token must differ.
overrides.costDescription: A token set by hand stops following the seed. The next brand change moves everything derived and leaves this value behind, and no audit reports it.
overrides.labelHelper: By default the label is chosen by the seed's own luminance, the same 0.179 threshold a runtime re-theme uses. Forcing it is the one override the generator has a flag for.
overrides.darkHelper: Contrast parity with the light theme puts it at {parity}. Hue and saturation are held either way; only lightness moves. An authored value is allowed to fail, and the table above is how it says so.
overrides.darkNoParity: No lightness at this hue and saturation clears both floors, so there is no parity value to depart from.

export.title: 5. Export
export.description: Paste the first block into your own theme file and the second over the baked email palette, which no stylesheet can reach.
export.divergesWhy: The dark seed's lightness was authored here. The generator searches for parity and has no flag for it, so no command reproduces this file.
export.noDarkTitle: This seed has no readable dark fill
export.noDarkDescription: No lightness at this hue and saturation clears both 4.5:1 on its own label and 3:1 on the dark canvas. Desaturate the seed, or force the label above and look again.

disabledReason.heading: 3 · disabledReason · the reason an action doesn't work comes before the action
disabledReason.why: A disabled button conveys no 'why' at all. That's why the reason is placed before the action in DOM order (WCAG 2.2 · 1.3.2), and the tile carries data-unavailable so its medallion recedes. disabledReason does not disable the button — that stays the consumer's own Button prop.

loadingCatalog.heading: 4 · Loading state and catalog entry
loadingCatalog.why: ServiceLauncherCardSkeleton is the initial placeholder with the same skeleton, requires a label, carries aria-busy, and deliberately never opens a live region. ServiceCatalogCta is the companion tile you place alongside it only when a real additional entry point exists, and it accepts a glyph other than the default Plus.

edgeCases.heading: 5 · Touching the edges · a 3-line name, no description, a long hostname that won't break
edgeCases.why: A tidy example never shows where a tile breaks. This is the side that breaks: a name that wraps to 3 lines sits next to a 2-word name in the same row, a tile with no description sits beside one that has one, and a hostname with no whitespace tries to stretch the column. If it looks unsightly, this section is doing its job — what has to hold up is the component, not the sample data.

A broken image never enters the DOM. The image box is the same 20px as the glyph (--card-service-launcher-icon-glyph-size), and its aspect ratio is preserved with object-fit: contain.

chartsDocs.areaSplitTitle: AreaChart · fill apart from stroke / cropped value axis
chartsDocs.areaSplitBody: series[].fillColor sets the band's colour independently of the line's color, and valueDomain / valueTicks state the value axis outright. A non-zero baseline is legitimate only where the SHAPE is the message and zero is not a meaningful reference — a price, a temperature, an index, a latency percentile. In any figure that asks the reader to compare magnitudes (every bar chart), it exaggerates the wobble and misleads. If you crop, say the range and keep the grid.
chartsDocs.tokenScopeTitle: Theme tokens · scoped to a region
chartsDocs.tokenScopeBody: Stroke weight, band density and grid dash are house style, so they are tokens rather than props. --chart-series-stroke-width / --chart-area-fill-alpha / --chart-grid-line-dash are set on the block below and nowhere else. No page-local CSS, no raw recharts.

page.subtitle: A themed region whose overlays keep the region's tokens.
page.title: ThemeScope

intro.title: Why a region needs this at all
intro.description: Every overlay portals to document.body, so custom-property inheritance stops at the portal boundary.
intro.body: A region that themes itself themes its own subtree and nothing it opens: measured on a scoped theme, the region read --primary 204 100% 37% and the Dialog it opened read 268.7 100% 50%, the package default. ThemeScope carries the computed difference between the region and the document root to a host at the portal destination, so the overlay inherits it by containment. It has no theme prop — it reads the DOM, which is why an inline style, a class and a stylesheet rule all behave the same.

glass.name: Glassmorphism
glass.note: Frosted translucent panels, a backdrop blur with saturation, a thin light edge and layered depth over a vivid ground.

flat.name: Flat
flat.note: No corners, no shadow, opaque surfaces separated by a line. Squaring one number costs sixty-seven declarations.

neubrutalism.name: Neubrutalism
neubrutalism.note: Thick black borders, hard offset shadows with no blur, square corners and loud saturated fills. Thickening a border costs 22 declarations and still reaches only a fifth of them.

section.typeNote: The ink ramp is the first thing a translucent surface breaks, so every step of it is on the page at once.
section.fieldsNote: A field has to read as a place you can type before it reads as a theme: fill, border, focus ring, placeholder and the filled and empty states are all here.
section.overlaysNote: These are opened by the measurement, not merely present. Each one portals out of this subtree and reaches the theme through ThemeScope's overlay host.
section.absentNote: An absence nobody can see is an absence nobody accounts for.

absent.provider: A provider, already mounted above this page by the preview runtime.
absent.overlayPortal: A provider that re-parents every overlay portal; mounting it here would replace the ThemeScope host this page exists to measure.
absent.themeScope: It is this page's own wrapper.
absent.ownsPage: A shell that owns the whole document; it cannot nest inside AppShell.
absent.hook: A hook. It has no surface of its own to paint.
absent.inertia: An Inertia adapter; it needs a router this preview does not have.
absent.needsFile: It needs a real File chosen from a file input.
absent.needsNetwork: It needs a network image; committed assets are used instead.
absent.needsRouter: It needs a route and a prefetchable query.
absent.needsQuery: It needs a live TanStack Query result, which is data rather than theme.
absent.invisible: It is on the page, and by definition it paints nothing.
absent.needsSchema: It needs a zod schema, and check:example-imports allows a docs page to import only react, lucide-react and @godxjp/ui.
absent.sameSurface: The composed form of AlertDialog, which is on the page; it paints no new surface.

treeDocs.spaceDescription: By default Space is Enter's twin: it selects. In a folder navigator whose selection loads a listing pane, every selection reloads it, so spaceAction="toggle" makes Space open or close the branch and nothing else (a lazy loadData fetch runs here too). Enter still selects, and on a leaf Space still selects. Focus the tree on the left and compare Space with Enter.
